body:
## Outcome
The original bounded Brownian concatenation problem remains **unsolved**. This partial proves an almost-sure approximation by fixed-origin two-sided Brownian motion with O(sqrt(log R)) uniform error on [-R,R], hence a two-sided diffusive scaling limit. It does not establish the exact finite random time shift required by the original definition.

## Scope and review
- Independent, not necessarily identically distributed, stopped Brownian pieces; a common deterministic duration bound and divergent sums in both directions
- Explicit treatment of zero durations and of the distinction between a fixed junction and a random time origin
- Piece-rotation mechanism credited to Burdzy and Scheutzow; no novelty or priority claim
- Separate adversarial review passed the unchanged frozen mathematical artifact, with the submitted and independent exact controls included

Two substantive attempts used. Actual author and reviewer model: gpt-6-astra, xhigh. This is a scoped partial research checkpoint, not a full solution.

Queue disposition: **unsolved**. The campaign's single queue writer will add the row update to this branch. This commit changes only this problem's attempt folder.

No merge or release is requested.
title: 9500008: reviewed Brownian approximation; random-shift target unresolved
